props.title: Pixelate Without the Drift

B10.capture_spec: C05: Lab sprite (teal sprite, fit scale), lab-shaders/06-pixelate-center.gdshader; blocks stepped 128, 64, 32, 16, 8, each held 1.6 s (8 s), 30 fps, Forward+, nearest filter. Verified still renders at all five values (06-center-n128 to n8-sprite-fit).
B10.visual_intent: Act title 'Pixelate Without the Drift' (serif 40) top-left. A real Godot render: the teal test sprite, smooth at first, then coarser in five steps until it is a chunky grid of blocks. Caption: 'pixelate: show a picture as big blocks'.
B10.motion_claim: The sprite loses detail in steps, each step a coarser grid of flat blocks.

show.event: act title, caption 'pixelate: show a picture as big blocks'; sprite at full detail
coarser steps as the voice says every pixel has the same color
chunkiest step held

B10.why: The beat names the goal; the real sprite going chunky is the goal, and the code comes next.

B11.visual_intent: A cell drawn as a four by four grid of pixel dots above a horizontal strip that stands for the picture (a teal-to-cream gradient bar). Sixteen thin curved lines run from the pixel dots down to ONE terracotta lookup point on the strip, with the words 'which spot?' beside it. Then the cell's pixels all take the one color found there. Label: 'one cell, one spot'. Midpoint still (45 to 55 %): all sixteen lines have converged on the one lookup point; the cell has not taken its color yet.
B11.motion_claim: All sixteen lines converge on a single point and the cell takes one color.

show.event: cell of pixels over the picture strip; the sixteen lines converge on one point (finished by 38 %)
the cell's pixels all take the one color found there; label 'one cell, one spot'
'which spot?' beside the point

B11.runner_up: ShaderLab render of a pixelated sprite
B11.why: Many pixels sending their lookups to one spot is a geometry of arrows; motion shows the convergence.

B12.capture_spec: C06: Lab sprite (fit scale), lab-shaders/05-pixelate-corner.gdshader, blocks = 16, still PNG. Verified: 16 blocks of 8 picture pixels each way.
B12.visual_intent: Code card at left (uniform blocks, the snapped address, the texture lookup); at right a real Godot window: the sprite pixelated into sixteen by sixteen blocks.
B12.motion_claim: The floor-and-divide line is highlighted, then the texture line, with the blocky sprite in the window.

show.event: snap line highlighted
texture line highlighted

B12.why: Code and its result side by side: one line of snapping and the picture is in blocks.

B13.capture_spec: C07: Lab sprite (fit scale), lab-shaders/05-pixelate-corner.gdshader, blocks = 16, no material until the voice says "It jumps" (about 36 % of the beat) then the shader is assigned (--material-at, set from the audio), about 12 s, 30 fps, Forward+, nearest filter. Verified (verify-patterns.py): the sprite's centre moves +3.5, +3.5 picture pixels at 8-pixel blocks (+7.5 at 16-pixel blocks, +1.5 at 4-pixel blocks): half a block, less the half-pixel of the measurement. At 50 %: shader on. At 85 %: shader on.
B13.visual_intent: Code card at left; at right a real Godot window: the plain teal sprite sits still for a few seconds with a terracotta ring (grey backing) on its silhouette, then the shader switches on and the sprite jumps down and to the right out of the ring. Readouts '3.5 px right' and '3.5 px down' land beside it.
B13.motion_claim: The sprite is still, then jumps down and to the right the moment the shader switches on.

show.event: plain sprite with a ring on its silhouette
shader switches on; the sprite jumps down and right
readouts: 3.5 px right, 3.5 px down

B13.runner_up: manim animation of an arrow shifting a sprite
B13.why: A real jump measured against a fixed ring is the evidence; a drawing would only illustrate it.

B14.visual_intent: One dimension, drawn large. A straight diagonal line (the picture, a ramp) over eight cells marked on the axis. A terracotta dot sits on the line at the left edge of each cell with a short drop line down to a flat tread: together the treads form a staircase under the line. A double-headed arrow shape between the line and the middle of a tread is labelled 'half a block'. Labels: 'the picture', 'what the blocks show'. Midpoint still (45 to 55 %): the line, the staircase and the double arrow 'half a block' are all settled; the two labels arrive after the midpoint.
B14.motion_claim: The lookup dots drop one by one, the staircase builds under the line, and the half-block gap is marked.

show.event: line over eight cells
lookup dots at each left edge drop to treads; staircase builds (finished by 33 %)
double arrow 'half a block' between line and tread middle (finished by 44 %)
labels 'the picture' and 'what the blocks show' appear

B14.why: A staircase lying half a step off the line is exactly 'arrives late by half a block'; the picture needs no pixels, so a clean one-dimensional drawing wins.

B15.capture_spec: C08: Lab sprite (fit scale), lab-shaders/06-pixelate-center.gdshader, blocks = 16, material assigned at the voice's 'Add one half' (about 25 % of the beat, --material-at, set from the audio), about 11 s, 30 fps, Forward+, nearest filter. B15.visual_intent: Code card at left (the snapped address now with + 0.5 added to the floor before the divide); at right the same scene: the plain sprite with its ring, then the shader switches on and the sprite turns blocky but stays inside the ring. Readout 'stays put'.
B15.motion_claim: The sprite turns blocky at the switch but does not move: it stays inside its ring.

show.event: plain sprite with ring
plus-half highlighted; the shader switches on, the sprite stays put
readout 'stays put'

B15.runner_up: manim animation of a sprite staying put
B15.why: A non-event needs a fixed reference: the ring that the earlier jump left makes 'stays put' visible.

B16.visual_intent: A number line from 0 to 1 cut into four cells (ticks at 0.25, 0.5, 0.75). A terracotta marker sits at the address 0.6. Beside it an arithmetic stack types in line by line (monospace): '0.6 × 4 = 2.4', 'floor gives 2' (a word, never an arrow glyph), '+ 0.5 = 2.5', '÷ 4 = 0.625'. The third cell (0.5 to 0.75) gets a heavy outline and a terracotta lookup dot lands at its middle, 0.625. Midpoint still (45 to 55 %): the stack shows '0.6 × 4 = 2.4' and 'floor gives 2'; the marker is at 0.6; the '+ 0.5' line has not typed yet.
B16.motion_claim: The marker's number is carried through the four steps and the lookup dot lands exactly in the middle of its cell.

show.event: number line, four cells, marker at 0.6
stack: floor gives 2
÷ 4 = 0.625; dot lands in the middle of the third cell

B16.why: A number carried through four operations and landing in a cell is arithmetic made visible; code alone hides the numbers.

B17.capture_spec: C09: Lab sprite (fit scale), lab-shaders/07-pixelate-round.gdshader, blocks = 16, still PNG. Verified: the sprite's centre -0.5, -0.5 px (no drift); the edge problem is not visible on the sprite (transparent padding) and is shown in B18 from the gradient run.
B17.visual_intent: Code card at left (the half is now inside the floor); at right a real Godot window: the sprite pixelated, centered where the original was, with the terracotta ring (grey backing) around the original silhouette.
B17.motion_claim: The plus-half is highlighted inside the floor while the sprite sits inside its ring: no drift.

show.event: floor(UV * blocks + 0.5) line highlighted
ring around the sprite: it did not move

B17.runner_up: manim code trace without the render
B17.why: The variant is code, and it looks right on the sprite: the real render with its ring is the honest 'looks fixed'.

B18.visual_intent: Two rows of blocks across a bracket labelled 'picture, 128 px' (the pixel-grid cast; outline cells with padding, no fill behind text). Top row, 'middle of the cell': sixteen equal blocks, each labelled 8 px at the first one. Bottom row, 'nearest grid line': the same grid shifted half a block, so seventeen blocks: the first and last are half width and wear terracotta rings with the label '4 px'; a middle block is labelled '8 px'. A small grey credit: 'Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · 16 blocks'. Midpoint still (45 to 55 %): both rows are settled: sixteen equal blocks above, seventeen blocks below with half-width ends; the rings arrive after the midpoint.
B18.motion_claim: The grid slides half a block and the first and last blocks are cut to half width inside their rings.

show.event: bracket and the top row of sixteen equal blocks
bottom row slides half a block; seventeen blocks, ends half width
rings on both end blocks: 4 px; a middle block: 8 px; credit line

B18.why: A row of blocks with the end cells cut in half is a pixel-grid picture; the dark corner of the real gradient render would also fail the type gate.
